### Brown County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-03-02 (confirmed by signed BoCC minutes, Book V Page 129)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-03-02` (exact)

- **Moratorium ID:** `ks-brown-county-2026`

- **Outcome:** Planning Commission to consider recommendations for regulation.

### Marion County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2026-03-02 (per Citizen Portal AI summary of the March 3, 2026 commission action)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-03-02` (exact)
- **Duration:** Through 2027-06-01: Resolution No. 2026-12 (adopted 2026-03-02) originally ran through 2026-06-01; the Marion County BoCC unanimously adopted Resolution No. 2026-19 on 2026-05-11, extending the moratorium for one additional year, through 2027-06-01. (A separate Feb. 17, 2026 action had adopted a one-year battery-energy-storage moratorium expiring March 1, 2027; commissioners had earlier discussed a one-year pause on data centers but initially adopted a three-month interim instrument before extending it to a full year.)
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, battery storage
- **Moratorium ID:** `ks-marion-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution No. 2026-12, "A Resolution Providing for a Temporary Moratorium on the Acceptance of Applications Relating to the Establishment, Operation or Expansion of Data Centers within the Unincorporated Areas of Marion County, Kansas," citing K.S.A. 12-741 et seq. and K.S.A. 19-101 et seq. police power; passed and adopted March 2, 2026 (unanimous, 5-0; signed by Chairman Dave Crofoot, attested by County Clerk Ashley Herpich, county seal affixed). Extended one year by Resolution No. 2026-19, "A Resolution Extending the Temporary Moratorium...," passed and adopted May 11, 2026 (unanimous, 5-0).
- **What prompted it:** County commissioners sought time to understand battery storage and data centers after presentations from Flint Hills Rural Electric Cooperative and Kansas Electric Power Cooperative; concerns included safety and protecting county residents.
- **Affected projects:** Data-center and related energy/discharge facilities exceeding 10 MW in unincorporated Marion County; staff stated the language excludes smaller stand-alone relay or hosting facilities.
- **Detailed status:** Active; extended through 2027-06-01 by Resolution No. 2026-19 (unanimous BoCC vote, adopted 2026-05-11).
- **Outcome:** Planning and zoning staff expected to prepare permanent rules.

### Sedgwick County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2026-01-14
- **Normalized date:** `2026-01-14` (exact)
- **Duration:** Initially 90 days through 2026-04-17 under Resolution 014-2026; on 2026-03-04 the BoCC voted unanimously to extend the moratorium to 2026-06-11; on 2026-05-06 (vote taken at the May 1, 2026 meeting per KWCH) the BoCC voted unanimously a second time to extend the moratorium to 2026-09-11
- **Current end date:** `2026-09-11`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ks-sedgwick-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution No. 014-2026 ("A Resolution Establishing an Interim Development Control and Providing for the Suspension of Certain Types of Use Applications and Building Permits"), adopted 2026-01-14, citing K.S.A. 12-741 et seq. and K.S.A. 19-101 et seq. police power (confirmed from the signed resolution PDF); extended by a BoCC resolution adopted 2026-03-04 (to 2026-06-11), and extended a second time by a BoCC resolution adopted 2026-05-06 (to 2026-09-11) [VERIFY extension resolution number]
- **What prompted it:** Wichita-Sedgwick County Unified Zoning Code did not define data centers; county had increased inquiries for potential projects, especially in unincorporated western Sedgwick County.
- **Affected projects:** Monarch Energy and NextEra Energy land-acquisition activity in western Sedgwick County; no filed applications identified at adoption.
- **Detailed status:** Active through 2026-09-11. After the initial 2026-03-04 extension (to 2026-06-11), the BoCC voted unanimously again on 2026-05-06 to extend the interim development control a second time, to 2026-09-11, at planning staff's request to satisfy Kansas's 20-day public-notice requirement before the Metropolitan Area Planning Commission considers new data-center zoning rules.
- **Outcome:** Wichita-Sedgwick County Metropolitan Area Planning Department prepared a data center white paper recommending definition, classification, conditional use review, overlay options, or prohibition of hyperscale facilities.
